explanation: Reptile lineages are classified based on the presence and number of openings (temporal fenestrae) behind the eye socket: 1) Anapsid (no opening) - turtles; 2) Diapsid (2 openings) - most reptiles and birds; and 3) Synapsid (1 opening) - mammals. Because most reptiles do not share a single unique common ancestor, Reptilia is considered a paraphyletic group rather than a monophyletic one. Crocodiles and birds are more closely related to dinosaurs than they are to lizards.

questions.q: Which skull lineage features one opening behind the eye socket and leads to mammals?
Why is the traditional class Reptilia considered paraphyletic rather than monophyletic?
opts: Reptiles do not have a single known common ancestor.
